As of April 16, 2026, I will keep doing what fits Quzhou best: one year of `winter wheat -> summer maize` on the same land. I am in the south of Hebei on the North China Plain, and this is still the main grain pattern here. Quzhou has large wheat area and local reporting from the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs and China Agricultural University still centers on winter wheat-summer maize rotation, with local high-yield demonstrations built around that system, not around switching to something unfamiliar. Sources: https://www.moa.gov.cn/ztzl/wcbgclz/qglb/202305/t20230522_6428066.htm , https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202406/t20240613_6457129.htm , https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/2/25/art_46232_1012984.html

I will not make my year complicated. I am 61, my schooling is limited, and I would rather do the crops I know how to manage steadily than chase a cash crop with more labor and more market risk. For wheat, I will use an improved local winter wheat variety, keep fertilizer moderate instead of heavy, water at the key times, and do simple disease-and-insect control, especially the usual late-season spray. For maize, I will sow right after wheat harvest, use hybrid seed, and use no-tillage direct seeding because the turnaround is tight and that is the normal Huang-Huai-Hai approach after wheat. The fertilizer numbers I am choosing are based on current official nutrient guidance for Hebei/southern North China wheat and Huang-Huai-Hai summer maize, but the exact irrigation count and target yield are my own judgment from those sources and from Quzhou’s water-saving, steady-yield direction. Sources: wheat fertilizer guidance https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/zxfb/202109/t20210916_6376525.htm and https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/zxfb/202209/t20220922_6411293.htm ; maize fertilizer guidance https://zzys.moa.gov.cn/tzgg/202303/t20230314_6423039.htm ; summer maize no-till seeding guidance https://njhs.moa.gov.cn/qcjxhtjxd/202306/t20230601_6429148.htm
